locations.facilities: Eight sound stages from 3,000 to 23,250 sq ft (Stage F 23,250 sq ft at 21 ft high, Stage H 21,000 sq ft at 43 ft), over 120,000 sq ft of creative space with 25,000 sq ft of production offices and 57,000 sq ft of support space; a 120,000-litre underwater tank with camera pit in Stage A, workshops, backlot areas, hair and makeup, props and wardrobe departments.
locations.suitability: Self-contained, secure 18-acre site with drive-in access on selected stages, meeting rooms and secure broadband; the on-site team offers space planning for interior and exterior sets.
locations.logistics: Herbert Road, Bray, County Wicklow, 12 miles south of Dublin; ample parking on site.

locations.name: Aughnanure Castle
locations.setting: Six-storey tower house of the O'Flaherty clan on a rocky outcrop above Lough Corrib near Oughterard in County Galway, with a banqueting hall and watchtower.

locations.name: Charles Fort
locations.setting: Star-shaped 17th-century coastal fortification above Kinsale harbour in west Cork, with bastions, gun batteries and barrack ruins overlooking the Atlantic approach.

locations.name: CHQ Building
locations.setting: Restored 1820 bonded warehouse on Custom House Quay in Dublin's docklands, now a glass-roofed hall with retail units, food outlets and hireable event and exhibition space.

locations.name: Cobh Heritage Centre
locations.setting: Emigration and maritime history exhibition in Cobh's former Victorian railway station, on the harbour town that was the Titanic's last port of call.

locations.name: Cork City Gaol
locations.setting: Restored 19th-century prison on a hillside above Cork city, with galleried cell blocks and warders' quarters, hired out for corporate events and filming or photo shoots.

locations.name: Cork City Hall
locations.setting: 1936 limestone civic building on the River Lee in Cork, with a domed concert hall, council chamber and function rooms available through the council's facilities-hire process.

locations.name: Derrynane House
locations.setting: Coastal home of nineteenth-century political leader Daniel O'Connell on the Ring of Kerry, with period rooms, a walled garden and dunes running down to the Atlantic.

locations.name: Donegal Castle
locations.setting: Restored 15th-century tower house and Jacobean wing in the centre of Donegal town, once the stronghold of the O'Donnell clan, on the banks of the River Eske.

locations.name: Doneraile Court
locations.setting: Georgian house and deer park in north Cork, with a walled garden, follies and grazing red deer, cared for by the Office of Public Works.

locations.name: Dublin Castle
locations.setting: Former seat of British administration in Ireland in central Dublin, with state apartments, a medieval tower, Georgian interiors and a courtyard used for state events.

locations.name: Dún Aonghasa
locations.setting: Prehistoric stone fort on a sheer cliff edge on Inishmore in the Aran Islands, with concentric ramparts and a defensive band of upright stones.

locations.name: Emo Court
locations.setting: Neoclassical domed mansion designed by James Gandon in County Laois, with formal lawns, a lake and an avenue of Wellingtonia trees, managed by the OPW.

locations.name: Glendalough
locations.setting: Early medieval monastic site in a glaciated Wicklow valley, with a round tower, ruined stone churches and two lakes, managed by the Office of Public Works.

locations.name: Killarney National Park
locations.setting: Ireland's first national park, around the Lakes of Killarney and the MacGillycuddy's Reeks mountains, with oak woodland, waterfalls and a resident red deer herd.

locations.name: Killruddery House
locations.setting: Elizabethan-revival mansion on the edge of Bray with a domed Victorian conservatory, formal gardens with twin canals, woodland walks and a working farmyard on the wider estate.
locations.known_for: Excalibur, My Left Foot, The Tudors, Fate: The Winx Saga

locations.name: Kilmainham Gaol
locations.setting: Preserved nineteenth-century prison with a galleried Victorian east wing, stone corridors and bare exercise yards, now a museum.
locations.known_for: The Italian Job (1969), In the Name of the Father, Paddington 2

locations.name: Lough Gur
locations.setting: Archaeological landscape around a horseshoe-shaped lake in County Limerick, with a Stone Age visitor centre, a stone circle and Iron Age hut sites.

locations.name: Pearse Museum & St Enda's Park
locations.setting: Former school run by Patrick Pearse in a Georgian house in Rathfarnham, south Dublin, set in a public park with woodland, a walled garden and a stream.

locations.name: Portumna Castle and Gardens
locations.setting: Early 17th-century semi-fortified house on Lough Derg in east Galway, with restored formal gardens, a kitchen garden and a woodland park managed by the OPW.

locations.name: Skellig Michael
locations.setting: Steep rocky island in the Atlantic off the Kerry coast, topped by a sixth-century monastic settlement of stone beehive huts.
locations.known_for: Star Wars: The Force Awakens, Star Wars: The Last Jedi

locations.name: Sligo Abbey
locations.setting: Ruined 13th-century Dominican friary in Sligo town, with a carved altar, cloister arcade and medieval tomb sculptures, open seasonally under the OPW.

locations.name: Strokestown Park House
locations.setting: Palladian-style Georgian house in County Roscommon set on about 300 acres, with a walled garden, the National Famine Museum and its own listed film location page.

locations.name: The Custom House Visitor Centre
locations.setting: Neoclassical 18th-century government building on the Liffey quays in Dublin, with a visitor centre in the vaulted basement telling the story of its construction and 1921 fire.

locations.name: The English Market
locations.setting: Covered Victorian food market in the centre of Cork, trading since 1788, with cast-iron arcades, fishmongers, butchers and a fountain courtyard; filming is arranged through Cork City Council.

locations.name: Trinity College Dublin
locations.setting: Ireland's oldest university, with cobbled squares, Georgian and Victorian quadrangles and the Long Room library, on a walled campus in the centre of Dublin.
locations.known_for: Educating Rita, Michael Collins, Circle of Friends

locations.name: Wicklow's Historic Gaol
locations.setting: Former county gaol in Wicklow town, in use from 1702 to 1924, with narrow cell blocks, a condemned cell and exercise yards preserved as a visitor attraction.

locations.name: Antico Caffè Greco
locations.setting: Coffee house on Via Condotti in Rome open since 1760, with a chain of small salons hung with paintings and 19th-century furnishings, among the city's oldest surviving interiors.

locations.name: Arena di Verona
locations.setting: 1st-century Roman amphitheatre in central Verona, its arena floor and stone tiers used since 1913 for outdoor opera performances every summer.

locations.name: Base Milano
locations.setting: Former Ansaldo machine works in Milan's Tortona district, converted into a co-working and cultural hub whose large industrial halls host exhibitions, fashion events and shoots.

locations.name: Belmond Hotel Cipriani
locations.setting: Hotel on Giudecca island in Venice with gardens, an outdoor pool and lagoon-facing rooms in a converted 16th-century building, reached from Saint Mark's Square by private launch.

locations.name: Bocconi University
locations.setting: Milan business university campus that includes the Grafton Architects-designed SDA building, with lecture halls, a library, courtyards and contemporary architecture around Via Sarfatti.

locations.name: Caffè Florian
locations.setting: Coffee house on Saint Mark's Square in Venice open since 1720, with a sequence of small decorated rooms, mirrors and painted panels largely unchanged since the 19th century.

locations.name: Campo Imperatore, Gran Sasso
locations.setting: High plateau beneath the Gran Sasso massif in Abruzzo, known locally as Italy's Little Tibet, with wide alpine grassland and a former ski hotel where Mussolini was briefly held in 1943.

locations.name: Cinecittà
locations.setting: Historic Rome studio complex founded in 1937, with sound stages including the vast Teatro 5 and permanent backlot sets such as ancient Rome.
locations.known_for: Ben-Hur (1959), La Dolce Vita (1960), Rome (2005-2007, HBO/BBC)
locations.facilities: 22 soundstages (24 planned) from 380 to 3,500 m2, the largest Stage 22 (3,500 m2) and Stage 5 (2,880 m2), each with dressing rooms, offices, makeup rooms and workshops; an LED volume in Stage 18 with a 452 m2 curved wall (8 m high, 52 m long), a 417 m2 motorised ceiling and a 25 m rotating platform; a backlot of nearly 10 hectares with power and water and permanent sets, plus set construction, film lab and audio and video post-production.
locations.suitability: Stages are soundproof, air conditioned and many have waterproof trapdoors for effects; they can be booked individually or in combination. Five new soundstages and four renovations are announced for 2026.

locations.name: Città della Scienza
locations.setting: Science museum and congress centre on the former Bagnoli industrial waterfront in Naples, with interactive exhibition halls, an auditorium and modular event spaces for hire.

locations.name: Craco
locations.setting: Abandoned hilltop town in Basilicata, evacuated after a 1963 landslide, with medieval stone houses, a tower and a church left standing on the exposed ridge.
locations.known_for: The Passion of the Christ (2004), Quantum of Solace (2008), Wonder Woman (2017)

locations.name: Fabbrica del Vapore
locations.setting: Former 19th-century tram and rail-carriage factory in Milan, now a municipal cultural centre with industrial brick halls and an outdoor yard used for exhibitions and events.

locations.name: Grand Hotel et de Milan
locations.setting: 1863 hotel in central Milan near La Scala, with period salons, an internal courtyard and rooms including the suite where composer Giuseppe Verdi lived and died.

locations.name: Grand Hotel Villa Serbelloni
locations.setting: Nineteenth-century lakeside hotel on the Bellagio promontory overlooking Lake Como, with period public rooms, terraced gardens and views over both branches of the lake.

locations.name: Grande Miniera di Serbariu
locations.setting: Former coal mine at Carbonia in Sardinia, its headframe, washery buildings and underground galleries preserved as a mining museum with period machinery and accessible tunnel sections.

locations.name: Ivrea, Industrial City of the 20th Century
locations.setting: Early to mid-20th-century Olivetti factory town in Piedmont, its rationalist and modernist office and social buildings along Via Jervis forming a UNESCO World Heritage industrial landscape.
locations.known_for: Adriano Olivetti: La forza di un sogno (2013 miniseries)

locations.name: Lingotto Rooftop Track and Pinacoteca Agnelli
locations.setting: Former Fiat car factory in Turin with a rooftop test track encircling the building, now containing exhibition halls, a hotel and the Pinacoteca Agnelli art gallery beneath a glass pavilion.

locations.name: Manifattura Tabacchi
locations.setting: Former state tobacco factory in Florence, redeveloped into a mixed district with courtyards, industrial-style halls and a dedicated events venue called Motel.

locations.name: Mercato Centrale Firenze
locations.setting: Nineteenth-century iron-and-glass covered market near San Lorenzo in Florence, with a ground-floor produce market and an upper-floor food hall of stalls and communal tables.

locations.name: Milano Centrale Railway Station
locations.setting: Monumental 1931 railway terminus in Milan with a vast steel-and-glass train shed, marble ticket halls and Art Deco and Assyrian-influenced decoration across several levels.

locations.name: Mole Antonelliana - National Cinema Museum
locations.setting: Nineteenth-century domed landmark in Turin housing the National Cinema Museum, with a spiral ramp, a central exhibition hall beneath the dome and a glass panoramic lift to the top.

locations.name: OGR Torino
locations.setting: Former 19th-century railway repair workshop in Turin, restored into a steel-and-glass exhibition and event hall with an attached production and rehearsal wing.

locations.name: Ortigia
locations.setting: Historic island core of Syracuse in Sicily, with a baroque cathedral built into the columns of a Greek temple, narrow lanes, a waterfront promenade and a Norman castle at its tip.

locations.name: Palazzo dei Congressi, EUR
locations.setting: Rationalist congress hall in Rome's EUR district, built for a cancelled 1942 world's fair, with a marble facade, a colonnaded portico and a large domed hall, managed by EUR SpA.

locations.name: Porticoes of Bologna
locations.setting: Covered walkways lining central Bologna's streets, including the roughly 3.8 km arcade climbing to the Sanctuary of San Luca, a UNESCO World Heritage arrangement of porticoes.

locations.name: Porto Antico di Genova
locations.setting: Nineteenth-century harbour warehouses and docks in Genoa, redeveloped for Expo 1992 into a waterfront of piazzas, a marina, an aquarium and event spaces along the old quays.

locations.name: Porto Vecchio di Trieste
locations.setting: Disused free port in Trieste with about seventy hectares of 19th-century warehouses, rail sidings and quays between the city centre and the sea, now under partial redevelopment.

locations.name: San Siro Stadium (Stadio Giuseppe Meazza)
locations.setting: Multi-tiered football stadium in Milan shared by AC Milan and Inter, with a distinctive spiral-ramp exterior and seating for over 75,000.

locations.name: Sassi di Matera
locations.setting: Ancient cave-dwelling districts carved into a limestone ravine, frequently standing in for biblical-era Jerusalem.
locations.known_for: The Passion of the Christ (2004), Wonder Woman (2017), No Time to Die (2021)

locations.name: Stadio Olimpico
locations.setting: Rome's main stadium in the Foro Italico complex, with tiered seating for over 70,000 used for football, athletics, concerts and other large events.

locations.name: Teatro alla Scala
locations.setting: 1778 opera house in central Milan with a gilded horseshoe auditorium, tiered boxes, a museum wing and a stage house used for opera, ballet and concerts.

locations.name: Teatro Massimo
locations.setting: Largest opera house in Italy, in central Palermo, with a neoclassical facade, a horseshoe auditorium seating around 1,300 and backstage and rehearsal spaces.

locations.name: Toledo Metro Station
locations.setting: Underground metro station in central Naples built around 40 metres deep, with a mosaic-lined vaulted concourse known as the Crater de Luz, part of the city's art-station network.

locations.name: Tropea
locations.setting: Clifftop town on Calabria's Tyrrhenian coast, with a historic centre of stone lanes and balconies overlooking the beach and the offshore Santa Maria dell'Isola sanctuary.

locations.name: Villa del Balbianello
locations.setting: Eighteenth-century villa on a wooded promontory of Lake Como with terraced gardens and open lake panoramas, now a FAI heritage property.
locations.known_for: Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (2002), Casino Royale (2006)

locations.name: Villa Necchi Campiglio
locations.setting: 1930s rationalist villa in central Milan designed by Piero Portaluppi, with period interiors, a garden, swimming pool and tennis court, run as a house museum by FAI.

locations.name: Blue Lagoon, Comino
locations.setting: Shallow turquoise channel between Comino and the islet of Cominotto, with white sand under clear water and low limestone cliffs on both shores.

locations.name: Dwejra
locations.setting: Rocky bay on Gozo's west coast with an inland sea joined to the open water by a natural tunnel, on a stretch of coastline once marked by the collapsed Azure Window.
locations.known_for: Game of Thrones (season 1), Clash of the Titans (2010)

locations.name: Fort Manoel
locations.setting: Baroque star fort built 1723 to 1755 on its own islet in Marsamxett Harbour, restored with bastions, a chapel and a large open parade ground used for big set builds.
locations.known_for: Assassin's Creed (2016), World War Z (2013), By the Sea (2015)

locations.name: Fort Ricasoli
locations.setting: Vast 17th-century bastioned fort at the mouth of the Grand Harbour whose open parade grounds host large-scale open-air set builds.

locations.name: Fort St Elmo
locations.setting: Star-shaped sixteenth-century fort at the tip of the Valletta peninsula, now home to the National War Museum, with bastions, a parade ground and sea-facing ramparts.

locations.name: Malta Film Studios
locations.setting: State-run studio facility whose two vast exterior water tanks sit on the shoreline so their surfaces blend into the natural sea horizon, complemented by an indoor insert tank.
locations.known_for: Raise the Titanic (1980), U-571 (2000), Captain Phillips (2013)

locations.name: Malta Maritime Museum
locations.setting: Former Royal Naval bakery on the Vittoriosa waterfront, now a museum of Malta's dockyards and Grand Harbour shipping history from the Knights to the twentieth century.
locations.known_for: Malta Story (1953, depicting the wartime dockyards)

locations.name: Manoel Theatre
locations.setting: Baroque theatre opened in 1732 in central Valletta, one of Europe's oldest still in use, with a gilded three-tier horseshoe auditorium seating around 620.

locations.name: Mdina
locations.setting: Walled medieval hilltop city of narrow honey-coloured limestone streets, baroque palaces and a monumental main gate.

locations.name: Palazzo Parisio
locations.setting: Eighteenth-century palace remodelled in the 1860s with gilded salons, frescoed halls and Italianate walled gardens with an orangery and grotto.
locations.suitability: The venue's own site lists filming among the activities it hosts, alongside weddings, product launches and fashion shows.

locations.name: Popeye Village
locations.setting: Wooden waterfront village built as the full-scale set for the 1980 Popeye musical, kept afterwards on Anchor Bay as a walk-through attraction.

locations.name: University of Malta
locations.setting: Main university campus at Tal-Qroqq, with lecture halls, a library and a mix of 1960s and later buildings spread over a hillside site near Msida.

locations.name: Valletta Design Cluster
locations.setting: Restored eighteenth-century Ospizio building in Valletta, later a hospital and armoury, now converted into shared workspaces and studios for Malta's creative economy.

locations.name: Valletta Historic Centre
locations.setting: UNESCO-listed sixteenth-century fortified capital on a narrow peninsula, its grid of limestone streets lined with baroque churches, auberges and balconied townhouses.
locations.known_for: World War Z (2013), Murder on the Orient Express (2017), By the Sea (2015)

locations.name: Valletta Waterfront
locations.setting: Row of restored eighteenth-century baroque warehouses along the Grand Harbour quayside, now a strip of restaurants, bars and shops beside the cruise terminal.

locations.name: Ahoy Rotterdam
locations.setting: Multi-hall arena and convention complex in Rotterdam-Zuid with a 16,000-capacity main arena, used for sport, concerts and the 2021 Eurovision Song Contest.

locations.name: Amsterdam Canal Ring
locations.setting: Seventeenth-century ring of tree-lined canals with gabled townhouses, humpback bridges and houseboats.
locations.known_for: The Fault in Our Stars, Ocean's Twelve

locations.name: Aviodrome
locations.setting: Aviation museum and heritage hangars at Lelystad Airport with historic aircraft including a DC-2, DC-3 and Fokker airliners on static and taxiway display.

locations.name: Bataviawerf (Batavialand)
locations.setting: Working historic shipyard in Lelystad building full-size replica VOC ships beside a reconstructed seventeenth-century harbour, sail loft and rigging sheds.
locations.suitability: Small shoots (up to 4 people) allowed during opening hours with 2 working days notice; larger productions get exclusive access outside opening hours with 10 working days notice

locations.name: Blokhuispoort
locations.setting: Former nineteenth-century prison in Leeuwarden with a star-shaped cell wing, converted into a cultural venue with a library, hostel and workspaces.

locations.name: Erasmusbrug
locations.setting: Asymmetric cable-stayed bridge with a 139-metre bent steel pylon spanning the Nieuwe Maas against the Rotterdam skyline.

locations.name: Euromast
locations.setting: 185-metre observation tower beside Rotterdam's Park, with a rotating Euroscoop deck near the top giving a panoramic view over the city and harbour.

locations.name: Fort bij Vechten
locations.setting: Nineteenth-century fortress of the New Dutch Waterline near Bunnik, with brick casemates, powder magazines and grass-covered ramparts around a moat.

locations.name: Forum Groningen
locations.setting: Contemporary multi-storey public library and culture building on Groningen's Grote Markt, with a rooftop terrace, cinema and stacked glass atria.

locations.name: Giethoorn
locations.setting: Car-free village of thatched farmhouses linked by canals, footbridges and punting boats in the Overijssel peatlands, part of the Weerribben-Wieden wetland.

locations.name: Hoge Veluwe National Park
locations.setting: A 5,400-hectare national park of drift sand, heathland and pine forest on the Veluwe, home to the Kroller-Muller Museum and free-roaming red deer and wild boar.

locations.name: Johan Cruijff ArenA
locations.setting: 55,000-seat retractable-roof stadium in Amsterdam Zuidoost, home to Ajax, with a bowl of tiered stands usable for matches, concerts and productions.

locations.name: Kinderdijk
locations.setting: UNESCO World Heritage polder landscape south-east of Rotterdam with nineteen eighteenth-century windmills lined along parallel waterways.

locations.name: Kruisherenhotel Maastricht
locations.setting: Fifteenth-century Gothic monastery church and cloister in Maastricht converted into a design hotel, keeping vaulted ceilings, stained glass and a choir loft.

locations.name: Kurhaus Den Haag
locations.setting: Grand 1885 beachfront hotel at Scheveningen with a domed Kurzaal ballroom of murals and chandeliers, and terraces facing the North Sea promenade.

locations.name: Lloyd Hotel
locations.setting: Former 1921 emigrant hotel on Amsterdam's eastern docklands, rebuilt with room categories from one to five stars mixing Art Deco and contemporary interiors.

locations.name: Loonse en Drunense Duinen
locations.setting: Inland drift-sand dune area of around 2,000 hectares between Tilburg and 's-Hertogenbosch, with open sand plains, marram grass and pine forest edges.

locations.name: Louis Hartlooper Complex
locations.setting: Former 1921 courthouse in Utrecht converted into an arthouse cinema and cafe, with a wood-panelled former courtroom now used as a screening room.

locations.name: Maeslantkering / Keringhuis
locations.setting: Giant swinging steel storm surge barrier at Hoek van Holland guarding the Nieuwe Waterweg, each of its two arms as long as the Eiffel Tower is high.

locations.name: Manteling van Walcheren
locations.setting: Dune woodland and beach reserve on the Walcheren coast near Domburg and Oostkapelle, combining old estate woods with open dunes and North Sea beach.

locations.name: Markthal Rotterdam
locations.setting: Arched 2014 market hall in Rotterdam with a horseshoe of apartments wrapped around a food market floor of stalls, restaurants and a barrel-vaulted ceiling mural.

locations.name: Media Park Hilversum
locations.setting: Television production campus in Hilversum with large audience studios such as Studio 21 and 22 and most national broadcasters on site.
locations.known_for: The Voice of Holland, The Voice Kids
locations.facilities: Studio 21 is offered as an event location with a 360 m2 LED screen, sound installation and light ceiling; the park houses over 100 media companies including NOS, RTL, NEP, EMG and ITV, with restaurants, a gym, a hair and makeup salon and childcare on site.
locations.suitability: A private business park without public opening hours; employees need a valid access pass and visitors are welcome around event start times. Studio specifications and rental terms are not published on the park's own site.
locations.logistics: Joop van den Endeplein 1, Hilversum: own railway station Hilversum Media Park with four trains an hour and a footbridge into the park; by car via A1 exit 9 Laren/Hilversum; 24-hour parking deck and garage A at EUR 2.00 per hour, card payment only.

locations.name: Museum Buurtspoorweg
locations.setting: Heritage narrow-gauge railway between Haaksbergen and Boekelo near the German border, with early twentieth-century steam trains and a period station building.

locations.name: Museum Steam Tram Hoorn-Medemblik
locations.setting: Heritage steam railway running 20 kilometres between Hoorn and Medemblik, with restored period carriages, a working locomotive shed and historic stations.

locations.name: NDSM Wharf
locations.setting: Former shipyard on the IJ in Amsterdam-Noord with a vast former assembly hall, dry docks and cranes, now used for events and creative work.

locations.name: NEMO Science Museum
locations.setting: Renzo Piano-designed green, ship-shaped science museum rising from the water at Amsterdam's Oosterdok, with a sloped public roof terrace and open exhibition floors.

locations.name: Netherlands Open Air Museum
locations.setting: Open-air heritage museum near Arnhem with more than 80 relocated historic Dutch buildings, farmhouses and windmills arranged as period villages around a working canal.

locations.name: Oosterscheldekering / Neeltje Jans
locations.setting: Nine-kilometre storm surge barrier across the Oosterschelde estuary with 62 movable steel gates on concrete piers, its visitor centre on the artificial island of Neeltje Jans.

locations.name: Pathe Tuschinski
locations.setting: 1921 Art Deco and Amsterdam School cinema on the Reguliersbreestraat, with an ornate auditorium, stained glass, mosaics and a sweeping foyer staircase.

locations.name: Philips Stadion
locations.setting: 35,000-seat home stadium of PSV in Eindhoven, with four continuous tiers of covered seating around the pitch.

locations.name: Radio Kootwijk
locations.setting: Isolated 1920s Expressionist transmitter hall on the Veluwe heathland, a monumental concrete radio station known as Building A, now used for events and productions.

locations.name: Rietveld Schroder House
locations.setting: UNESCO-listed 1924 De Stijl house in Utrecht by Gerrit Rietveld, with sliding partition walls, primary-colour accents and a flexible open first floor.

locations.name: Sint-Pietersberg / ENCI Quarry
locations.setting: Former limestone quarry on the southern edge of Maastricht, now a reclaimed nature area of white marl cliffs, terraces and a lake beside the old cement works.

locations.name: Sonneveld House
locations.setting: Fully furnished 1933 Nieuwe Bouwen villa in Rotterdam with period Functionalist interiors, tubular steel furniture and built-in fittings kept intact.

locations.name: SS Rotterdam
locations.setting: 1959 ocean liner of the Holland America Line permanently moored in Rotterdam, kept with original Art Deco and mid-century interiors, now a hotel and museum ship.

locations.name: Strijp-S
locations.setting: Former closed Philips factory campus in Eindhoven redeveloped into a creative district of brick industrial halls, courtyards and new residential towers.

locations.name: Thialf
locations.setting: Indoor 400-metre speed skating arena in Heerenveen with tiered seating for around 12,500 spectators, also used for concerts and events on the ice floor.

locations.name: Van Nelle Factory
locations.setting: UNESCO-listed 1931 factory in Rotterdam built for processing coffee, tea and tobacco, with steel-framed glass curtain walls and an elevated conveyor bridge.

locations.name: Veenhuizen Prison Museum
locations.setting: Former nineteenth-century penal colony building in Veenhuizen, part of the UNESCO Colonies of Benevolence, with cell blocks, courtyards and institutional corridors.

locations.name: Veluwsche Stoomtrein Maatschappij
locations.setting: Heritage steam and diesel railway between Apeldoorn and Dieren through Veluwe forest, with a restored 1887 station and period rolling stock at Beekbergen.

locations.name: Westergasfabriek
locations.setting: Former nineteenth-century coal gasworks in Amsterdam converted into an events site with several brick halls, a cobbled courtyard and a surrounding park.

locations.name: Wilhelminabrug
locations.setting: Steel arch road bridge over the IJssel at Deventer, used as the stand-in Arnhem bridge for the 1977 film A Bridge Too Far because the real bridge's surroundings had changed too much.

locations.name: Zonnestraal Sanatorium
locations.setting: Modernist 1928 former tuberculosis sanatorium near Hilversum by architect Jan Duiker, with steel-framed pavilions, large glass walls and a wooded park setting.

locations.name: Zuid-Limburgse Stoomtrein Maatschappij
locations.setting: Heritage steam railway through the South Limburg hills between Simpelveld, Kerkrade and Vetschau, with vintage carriages and period station buildings.

locations.name: Akershus Fortress
locations.setting: Medieval castle on Oslo's harbour promontory, expanded into an 18th-century bastioned fortress, with a stone keep, cobbled courtyards and government reception rooms still in ceremonial use.

locations.name: Atlantic Ocean Road
locations.setting: Eight-kilometre stretch of County Road 64 hopping between skerries on a chain of bridges, including the curved Storseisundet Bridge, exposed to open sea on both sides.

locations.name: Bastøy Prison
locations.setting: Low-security island prison in the Oslofjord run on an open, self-sufficient farming regime, with wooden former manor buildings alongside newer institutional blocks.
locations.known_for: King of Devil's Island (2010), Where to Invade Next (2015), Sicko (2007, DVD extras)

locations.name: Dagslys Studios
locations.setting: Five purpose-built stages from 81 to 500 square metres in Nydalen, Oslo, with lighting and grip rental, workshops, props storage and costume and makeup rooms in the same building.
locations.facilities: Five studios of 500, 211, 137, 124 and 81 m2 with shared makeup and costume fitting areas, showers, a dining space for 30, art department and props storage, a carpentry workshop and production offices; lighting, camera, generator and truck rental in the same building.
locations.suitability: Studios and equipment are rented for any media and film production, with 24-hour equipment delivery; part of Oslo Film Studios.
locations.logistics: Gjerdrums vei 6, Nydalen, Oslo

locations.name: Håkonshallen
locations.setting: Stone royal reception hall built in the 1250s inside Bergenhus fortress, rebuilt after a 1944 harbour explosion, with a vaulted timber-roofed great hall used for concerts and ceremonies.

locations.name: Hamar Cathedral Ruins (Domkirkeodden)
locations.setting: Ruins of a medieval stone cathedral on a headland by Lake Mjøsa, enclosed since 1998 in a modern glass and steel protective dome, part of a wider open-air history museum site.

locations.name: Hartvig Nissen School
locations.setting: Working upper secondary school building from 1899 in Oslo's Frogner district, a brick institutional building with classrooms and a courtyard used as the real setting for a teen drama series.

locations.name: Njardarheimr Viking Valley
locations.setting: Reconstructed Viking-age settlement of turf-roofed timber longhouses and workshops at the head of Nærøyfjorden, built and staffed as a living-history village.

locations.name: Odda Public Swimming Pool
locations.setting: Indoor municipal swimming pool in the former industrial town of Odda at the head of the Sørfjord, run as a public bathhouse with scheduled sessions for the local community.

locations.name: Preikestolen (Pulpit Rock)
locations.setting: Flat granite cliff ledge about 600 metres above Lysefjord, reached only by a four-kilometre mountain hiking trail.

locations.name: Sagene Folkebad
locations.setting: Indoor public bathhouse from 1899 in late-historicist style beside the Akerselva river, with arched windows and a period stair hall, still operating as a pool and rehabilitation facility.

locations.name: Stavanger Swimming Hall
locations.setting: Municipal indoor pool completed in 1971 next to Stavanger city hall, built in exposed concrete with a 25-metre pool, diving tower and separate children's pool.

locations.name: Vemork
locations.setting: Former hydroelectric and heavy-water plant on a gorge above Rjukan, with a monumental early-20th-century industrial facade, now a museum reached by cable car or an 8 km sabotage trail.
locations.known_for: Kampen om tungtvannet (1948), The Heroes of Telemark (1965), Kampen om tungtvannet / The Saboteurs (TV series, 2015)

locations.name: Vinje Church
locations.setting: Wooden cross-shaped parish church built in 1796 in the rural Vinje valley, seating around 225, with a painted interior altarpiece and carved benches from the 1930s.

locations.name: Alvernia Studios
locations.setting: A domed studio complex near Krakow with multiple sound stages and a large blue-screen hall, built on a former limestone quarry site 18 kilometres from Krakow Airport.

locations.name: ATM Studio
locations.setting: Film and television production centre of around 14,000 square metres in Warsaw's Wawer district, with multiple soundstages, TV studios, production offices and post-production facilities.
locations.known_for: The Voice of Poland, Dancing with the Stars: Taniec z gwiazdami
locations.facilities: Six halls totalling 5,200 m2: Hall A 1,500 m2 (45 x 34 m, 12 m high), Halls B to E 800 m2 each (32 x 25 m, 6 to 7 m high) and Hall F 500 m2; 14 dressing rooms of 34 m2 and two VIP dressing rooms of 60 m2, eight makeup rooms, scenic warehouses of 110 to 440 m2, a 3,900 kg cargo lift, catering and conference rooms on a 14,000 m2 site.
locations.suitability: Offers set design and construction, lighting and sound, post-production and VFX, costume and prop rental, OB vans and a virtual studio; two 4 MVA transformer stations, per-hall power connections from 16 A to 400 A, fibre links for nationwide TV transmission and silent ventilation for sound recording. Quotes on request.
locations.logistics: Wal Miedzeszynski 384, Wawer district, about 12 km from Warsaw city centre; three independent parking areas.

locations.name: Centennial Hall
locations.setting: A UNESCO-listed 1913 reinforced-concrete domed hall in Wroclaw, seating up to 6,000 beneath a 42-metre ribbed concrete dome, set in surrounding park and garden grounds.

locations.name: EC1 Lodz
locations.setting: A former coal-fired power station of 1907 in central Lodz, restored as a science and culture centre with its original turbine hall, boiler house and control rooms intact.

locations.name: Gdansk Shipyard (European Solidarity Centre)
locations.setting: The historic Lenin Shipyard gate and slipways where the Solidarity movement began in 1980, bordered by the European Solidarity Centre's rusted-steel museum building and surviving shipyard halls.

locations.name: Hala Koszyki
locations.setting: A 1908 steel-framed market hall in Warsaw's Ochota district, restored behind its original facade into a food hall of restaurants, bars and shops around a glazed central nave.

locations.name: Hel Peninsula
locations.setting: A 35-kilometre sand spit enclosing the Bay of Gdansk, with pine-backed Baltic beaches on its open-sea side and a historic fishing town and former naval base at its tip.

locations.name: Historic Guido Coal Mine
locations.setting: A former working coal mine in Zabrze, now a branch of the Museum of Coal Mining, with underground tours down to 320 metres and a preserved pithead machine hall.

locations.name: Kasprowy Wierch Cable Car
locations.setting: A 1936 aerial cableway climbing from Kuznice to the 1,987-metre summit of Kasprowy Wierch in the Tatras, run in two stages with a mid-station at Myslenickie Turnie.

locations.name: Kazimierz, Kraków
locations.setting: Kraków's former Jewish quarter, where synagogues, cobbled lanes and tenement courtyards still follow the pre-war street layout.

locations.name: Manufaktura
locations.setting: Izrael Poznanski's 19th-century red-brick textile mill complex in Lodz, converted into a shopping, leisure and museum quarter around its original factory yard and chimney.

locations.name: Nikiszowiec
locations.setting: A brick workers' housing estate built 1908-1918 for the Giesche coal mine, its enclosed courtyard blocks, arcaded passages and communal bakery still inhabited today.

locations.name: Nowa Huta
locations.setting: A planned socialist-realist steelworkers' town built from 1949 beside the former Lenin steelworks, with a monumental central square, arcaded avenues and uniform apartment blocks.

locations.name: Ogrodzieniec Castle
locations.setting: Ruined 14th-century castle on the highest hill of the Kraków-Częstochowa Upland, its broken towers rising among limestone outcrops on the Trail of the Eagles' Nests.

locations.name: Opera Lesna (Sopot Forest Opera)
locations.setting: An open-air amphitheatre cut into wooded dunes above Sopot, seating around 4,300 beneath a part-covered stage, home to the annual Sopot Festival.

locations.name: ORP Blyskawica
locations.setting: A Grom-class destroyer launched in 1936 and preserved as a museum ship on Gdynia's waterfront, with its bridge, gun turrets and below-deck compartments open to visitors.

locations.name: Palace of Culture and Science
locations.setting: A 237-metre socialist-classicist tower built in 1955 as a gift from the Soviet Union, holding theatres, cinemas, a congress hall, museums and an observation deck over central Warsaw.

locations.name: PGE Narodowy
locations.setting: Warsaw's national stadium of 2011, built on the site of the former Tenth-Anniversary Stadium, with a retractable roof and a facade patterned on the Polish flag.

locations.name: Poznan Town Hall
locations.setting: A Renaissance town hall of 1560 on Poznan's Old Market Square, rebuilt to Italian designs, with an arcaded facade, a mechanical clock with butting goats and a council chamber now a history museum.

locations.name: Spodek
locations.setting: A saucer-shaped 1971 sports and concert arena in central Katowice, its suspended roof spanning a hall seating up to about 11,500 for events.

locations.name: Stadion Slaski
locations.setting: A bowl stadium built in 1956 on a reclaimed slag heap in Chorzow, rebuilt with a membrane roof and seating around 54,000 for football, speedway and concerts.

locations.name: Warsaw Uprising Museum
locations.setting: A former tram power station on Wola's Przyokopowa street, converted into a museum of the 1944 uprising, retaining its brick turbine hall and machinery among the exhibition spaces.

locations.name: Wieliczka Salt Mine
locations.setting: A working salt mine near Krakow dating to the 13th century, its tunnels reaching over 300 metres deep and including carved underground chapels and chambers open to visitors.
locations.known_for: On the Silver Globe (1988), Spellbinder: Land of the Dragon Lord (1997)

locations.name: Alfama
locations.setting: Lisbon's oldest quarter, a hillside maze of steep cobbled lanes, tiled facades and tram lines above the Tagus.

locations.name: Algarve International Circuit
locations.setting: FIA-grade motor racing circuit near Portimao with elevation changes of up to forty metres, a start-finish straight, paddock buildings and grandstands.

locations.name: Barbadinhos Steam Pumping Station
locations.setting: Steam-powered water pumping station in Xabregas that operated from 1880 to 1928, preserving four steam engines inside its industrial hall as part of Lisbon's water museum.

locations.name: Braga Municipal Stadium
locations.setting: Football stadium built into a disused granite quarry on Monte Castro, with seating on two sides only and the bare quarry rock face left exposed behind each goal.

locations.name: Casa da Musica
locations.setting: Angular concrete concert hall by Rem Koolhaas on Porto's Rotunda da Boavista, with a shoebox-shaped main auditorium and several smaller performance rooms.

locations.name: Casa de Mateus
locations.setting: Baroque manor house near Vila Real with formal box-hedge gardens and a cedar tunnel, pictured on the label of Mateus Rose wine and used as a venue for concerts and cultural events.

locations.name: Casa dos Patudos
locations.setting: Early twentieth-century manor house in Alpiarca designed by architect Raul Lino for collector Jose Relvas, with period interiors and furnishings now open as a museum.

locations.name: Convento de Cristo
locations.setting: Templar castle and convent complex crowned by the round Charola oratory, with Manueline cloisters and hilltop ramparts above Tomar.
locations.known_for: The Man Who Killed Don Quixote (2018)

locations.name: Estacao do Rossio
locations.setting: Neo-Manueline railway station on Lisbon's Rossio square, with two horseshoe-arched doorways on its facade and platforms reached through a tunnel under the Bairro Alto hill.

locations.name: Evora Historic Centre
locations.setting: UNESCO-listed Alentejo city within Roman and medieval walls, with a Roman temple, whitewashed streets, a granite cathedral and the bone-lined Capela dos Ossos.

locations.name: Farol dos Capelinhos
locations.setting: Coastal lighthouse on Faial partly buried by ash from the 1957-58 Capelinhos submarine volcanic eruption, standing on the new lava and ash landscape it created.

locations.name: Lousal Mining Museum
locations.setting: Former pyrite-mining village in Grandola built around a twentieth-century mining company's power plant, now a museum with mining machinery, tools and worker housing.

locations.name: LX Factory
locations.setting: Former nineteenth-century textile and printing factory complex in Alcantara, now industrial halls, courtyards and a rooftop rented out as creative studios and event and shoot space.

locations.name: Madeira Botanical Garden
locations.setting: Terraced hillside garden above Funchal with exotic and native plant collections on volcanic slopes, reached by road or by a cable car from Monte.

locations.name: Marvao
locations.setting: Walled hilltop village on the Spanish border in the Serra de Sao Mamede, with a castle, whitewashed houses and long views over the surrounding plain.

locations.name: Mercado do Bolhao
locations.setting: Porto's historic municipal market, reopened in 2022 after renovation, with two levels of fish, meat, flower and grocery stalls under a restored iron and glass roof.

locations.name: Museu Nacional Ferroviario
locations.setting: National railway museum on the site of Entroncamento's railway works, with steam locomotives, carriages and workshop sheds spanning more than a century of Portuguese rail history.

locations.name: Portalegre Tapestry Museum (Guy Fino)
locations.setting: Tapestry museum inside a former noble town house in Portalegre, remodelled to display the local tapestry workshop's collection and archive alongside the original architecture.

locations.name: Praia do Guincho
locations.setting: Wide Atlantic surf beach backed by dunes and the Sintra hills, known for strong wind and heavy waves.

locations.name: Quinta do Pisao
locations.setting: Former farm estate on the edge of the Sintra-Cascais Natural Park, with old agricultural buildings, pine woods, pasture and a small lake open to visitors.

locations.name: Santa Cruz Municipal Aerodrome
locations.setting: Small municipal airfield close to the Santa Cruz beaches near Torres Vedras, home to the local aeroclub and one of the earliest civil aviation sites near Lisbon.

locations.name: University of Coimbra (Paco das Escolas)
locations.setting: UNESCO-listed royal-palace-turned-university courtyard in Coimbra, with the Joanina Baroque library, a bell tower and ceremonial halls still in academic use.

locations.name: Almaden Mining Park
locations.setting: A former mercury mine in Ciudad Real with headframes, shafts and underground galleries open for visits, worked from Roman times until closure in 2001.

locations.name: Anden 0 (Chamberi Ghost Station)
locations.setting: A disused 1919 Madrid Metro station preserved with its original tiled advertisements and platform furniture, opened to the public as a small museum called Anden 0.

locations.name: Antigua Carcel de Segovia
locations.setting: A former provincial prison in Segovia's old town, its cell blocks and courtyard converted into a cultural and exhibition centre.

locations.name: Auditorio de Tenerife
locations.region: Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Canary Islands
locations.setting: A sail-shaped concert hall on the Santa Cruz de Tenerife waterfront designed by Santiago Calatrava, with a curved white concrete shell around the main auditorium.

locations.name: Azkuna Zentroa
locations.setting: A former wine and grain warehouse, the Alhondiga, in Bilbao rebuilt by Philippe Starck behind its original brick facade, with 43 varied columns under a rooftop pool and terrace.

locations.name: Bardenas Reales
locations.setting: A semi-desert badlands landscape in southern Navarre with eroded clay buttes, plateaus and canyons, crossed by marked tracks inside a managed nature reserve.

locations.name: Belchite (old town)
locations.setting: The ruined shell of a town destroyed in the 1937 Battle of Belchite, left standing as a memorial with intact facades, a bell tower and rubble-filled streets open to visitors.
locations.known_for: The Adventures of Baron Munchausen (1988), Pan's Labyrinth (2006)

locations.name: Bilbao Metro
locations.setting: A metro network known for Norman Foster's glass-tube station entrances, locally called fosteritos, running through Bilbao and under the Nervion estuary.

locations.name: Bombas Gens
locations.setting: A former water-pump factory in Valencia built in Art Deco style, its restored halls now an art foundation with gallery and workshop spaces.

locations.name: Camp Nou
locations.setting: FC Barcelona's stadium in the Les Corts district, one of Europe's largest football grounds, with tiered stands, a museum and tour access during redevelopment.

locations.name: Canfranc International Railway Station
locations.setting: A Beaux-Arts railway station in the Pyrenees built for a cross-border line to France, its platforms and grand hall largely disused since 1970 and now under partial restoration.

locations.name: City of Arts and Sciences
locations.setting: A cluster of white concrete and glass structures by Santiago Calatrava and Felix Candela beside the old Turia riverbed, including a planetarium dome, an opera house, a science museum and an oceanarium.

locations.name: City of Culture of Galicia
locations.setting: A hilltop complex of curved stone and glass buildings by Peter Eisenman above Santiago de Compostela, combining library, museum and archive functions on wide open plazas.

locations.name: Ciudad de la Luz
locations.setting: Purpose-built studio complex beside the Mediterranean on the edge of Alicante, with large sound stages, exterior water tanks and production support buildings, reopened to shoots in 2022.
locations.known_for: Asterix at the Olympic Games (2008), The Impossible (2012)
locations.facilities: Six sound stages from 1,620 to 2,340 m2 (Plato 3: 2,340 m2 and 2,000 kVA; Plato 4: 1,794 m2; Platos 1, 2, 5 and 6: 1,620 m2, 12.5 m high, 10 x 8 m door, 1,250 kVA), interior tanks in Platos 3 and 5; an exterior 100 x 80 m water tank (8,000 m2, 1.2 m base, 5.2 m in a 30 x 30 m pit, 120 x 12 m green screen) with an infinity horizon to the Mediterranean; Backlot 1 of 42,367 m2 and Backlot 2 of 75,246 m2, each with 4,000 kVA; production buildings, workshops, storage, auditorium and post-production.
locations.suitability: Stages have NC-25 acoustic insulation and silent air conditioning; the tank offers up to 16 m underwater visibility, wave and water cannon systems and fills in 48 hours. 24-hour private security and access control let production teams work at any hour.
locations.logistics: On the edge of Alicante; the site cites an international airport nearby and Madrid under two hours by AVE high-speed train.

locations.name: Ciudad Encantada
locations.setting: A karst rock park near Cuenca where erosion has carved limestone into towers and shapes along a signed walking route through pine forest.

locations.name: Complutense University of Madrid
locations.setting: A large 1930s university campus, Ciudad Universitaria, west of central Madrid, with monumental faculty buildings, an observatory and open lawns.

locations.name: Conde Duque
locations.setting: A former 18th-century army barracks in Madrid with a long baroque facade and large parade-ground courtyards, converted into a public cultural centre.

locations.name: Corralejo Dunes Natural Park
locations.setting: A protected dune field and beach on the north coast of Fuerteventura, with shifting white sand hills managed by the island council.

locations.name: Euskalduna Palace
locations.setting: A congress and concert hall in Bilbao built in weathered steel on the site of the former Euskalduna shipyard, its shape referencing a ship's hull under construction.

locations.name: Fabra i Coats
locations.setting: A former 19th-century textile mill in Barcelona's Sant Andreu district, its long brick sheds and chimney now used as artist studios and a cultural centre.

locations.name: Gran Teatre del Liceu
locations.setting: Barcelona's main opera house on La Rambla, with a gilded horseshoe auditorium, a grand foyer and a stage house rebuilt after a 1994 fire.

locations.name: Hospital de Sant Pau
locations.setting: A former working hospital in Barcelona built as a campus of Art Nouveau pavilions with domes, mosaics and underground connecting tunnels, now a monument and event venue.

locations.name: Las Medulas
locations.setting: A red-cliffed landscape left by Roman open-cast gold mining, honeycombed with tunnels and covered in chestnut trees, managed as a protected heritage site in the Bierzo hills.

locations.name: Matadero Madrid
locations.setting: A former municipal slaughterhouse and cattle market beside the Manzanares river, its early 20th-century brick pavilions converted into galleries, studios and event spaces.

locations.name: Mercado Central de Valencia
locations.setting: A 1928 Art Nouveau market hall in central Valencia with domed ceilings, stained glass and stalls trading under an iron and tile structure.

locations.name: Mercado de San Miguel
locations.setting: A restored early 1900s cast-iron and glass market hall next to Plaza Mayor in Madrid, now a covered food and tapas market.

locations.name: Mini Hollywood (Oasys Parque Tematico)
locations.setting: A preserved western film set in the Tabernas desert built for 1960s Spaghetti Westerns, with a saloon, jail and main street still used for stunt shows and shoots.
locations.known_for: A Fistful of Dollars (1964), For a Few Dollars More (1965)

locations.name: Museo del Ferrocarril de Madrid
locations.setting: Spain's railway museum, housed in the former Delicias terminus with its 19th-century iron and glass trainshed, displaying historic locomotives and carriages.

locations.name: Palacio de Cibeles / CentroCentro
locations.setting: Madrid's ornate former post office building on Plaza de Cibeles, now the city hall, with a public exhibition centre, a rooftop viewpoint and a domed central hall.

locations.name: Palau de la Musica Catalana
locations.setting: A Modernista concert hall in Barcelona by Lluis Domenech i Montaner, with a stained-glass skylight, sculpted facades and an ornate main auditorium.

locations.name: Playa de las Catedrales
locations.setting: A tidal beach at Ribadeo shaped by sea arches and cliffs up to 30 metres high, fully walkable only at low tide and reached with a free timed permit in summer.

locations.name: Plaza de Toros de Las Ventas
locations.setting: Madrid's Neo-Mudejar bullring seating over 23,000, with brick and ceramic tile facades, tiered stands and an on-site bullfighting museum.

locations.name: Real Alcázar of Seville
locations.setting: Mudéjar royal palace complex in central Seville with tiled courtyards, arched ceremonial halls and lush formal gardens.
locations.known_for: Lawrence of Arabia (1962), Kingdom of Heaven (2005), Game of Thrones (season 5, Dorne)

photo.author: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA. Edited by MenkinAlRire

locations.name: Riotinto Mining Park
locations.setting: An open-cast copper and mineral mining landscape in Huelva province with reddened terrain, a heritage mining railway and a mining museum.

locations.name: Royal Tapestry Factory
locations.setting: A working tapestry and carpet workshop in Madrid founded in 1721, still weaving on wooden looms in its original workshop halls, open for guided tours.

locations.name: Santiago Bernabeu Stadium
locations.setting: Real Madrid's stadium in central Madrid, seating over 80,000 under a retractable roof, with dressing rooms, a trophy room and pitch-level tour access.

locations.name: Soller Railway
locations.setting: A narrow-gauge heritage railway on Mallorca linking Palma to Soller through the Serra de Tramuntana, still running vintage wooden carriages dating from 1912.

locations.name: Tabakalera
locations.setting: A former state tobacco factory in San Sebastian, its early 20th-century industrial halls converted into a contemporary culture and creation centre.

locations.name: Tabernas Desert
locations.setting: Europe's only true desert, with eroded badlands, dry riverbeds and surviving western town sets from the spaghetti-western era.
locations.known_for: Lawrence of Arabia (1962), The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (1966), Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade (1989)

locations.name: Timanfaya National Park
locations.setting: A national park on Lanzarote covering volcanic terrain formed by 18th-century eruptions, with lava fields, craters and a visitor route by coach.

locations.name: Tower of Hercules
locations.setting: A still-operating Roman lighthouse on a headland outside A Coruna, the oldest lighthouse in continuous use in the world, refaced in granite in the 18th century.

locations.name: University of Alcala
locations.setting: A 16th-century university campus in Alcala de Henares, centred on the Colegio de San Ildefonso with its plateresque facade and a historic assembly hall.

locations.name: University of Salamanca
locations.setting: Spain's oldest university, with a 16th-century plateresque facade, cloisters and historic lecture halls set around Salamanca's old town.

locations.name: University of Seville (Rectorado)
locations.setting: Seville's university rectorate housed in the former Royal Tobacco Factory, an 18th-century industrial building with long stone facades, courtyards and vaulted halls.

locations.name: Vizcaya Bridge
locations.setting: A working transporter bridge over the Ria de Bilbao between Portugalete and Las Arenas, carrying a suspended gondola across the estuary since 1893, with a walkway on top.

locations.name: Abisko National Park
locations.setting: National park in Swedish Lapland around Lake Tornetrask, with birch forest, mountain heath, the Abisko canyon and a mountain station used as a base for hiking and aurora viewing.

locations.name: Dalhalla
locations.setting: Open-air amphitheatre built into a flooded former limestone quarry near Rattvik in Dalarna, with a stage, restaurant and glamping accommodation beside the water.
locations.facilities: Restaurant, glamping tents, transfer buses for events

locations.name: Falu Gruva (Falun Mine)
locations.setting: UNESCO-listed copper mine in Falun, Dalarna, with underground tour routes, a mine museum, historic miners' cottages and a large open pit.

locations.name: Fårö
locations.setting: Small Baltic island north of Gotland with limestone rauk stacks, shingle shores and windswept heathland, where Ingmar Bergman lived and filmed for decades.
locations.known_for: Persona (1966), Through a Glass Darkly (1961), Scenes from a Marriage (1973)

locations.name: Film i Väst
locations.setting: Regional film fund and studio base in Trollhättan, nicknamed Trollywood, whose stages and industrial halls have held full-scale purpose-built sets.
locations.price_note: Studio Fares SEK 25,000 for the first day and SEK 20,000 per following day, plus 25 percent VAT (own site)
locations.facilities: Studio Fares: one 1,100 m2 sound stage (31.3 x 36.1 m, 10 m to the gallery) with a telfer system of 40 hoists, 1,000 A permanent power plus 1,000 A temporary, and doors 4.5 m high; props storage, carpentry workshop, production offices with 26 desks on two floors, three dressing rooms, makeup and wardrobe and a 50-seat cafe with kitchen.
locations.suitability: Rented primarily to Film i Vast co-productions under a licence agreement; external bookings are accepted at most two months ahead. The rent includes utilities, parking, cleaning and use of the facilities.
locations.logistics: Trollhattan; gated, secure parking with four EV charging points. Website in Swedish only.

locations.name: Icehotel
locations.setting: Hotel rebuilt each winter from ice and snow from the Torne River in Jukkasjarvi, Swedish Lapland, alongside a year-round warm wing, with conference and wedding facilities.
locations.facilities: Conference and events facilities, weddings program

locations.name: Kulturhuset Stadsteatern
locations.setting: Culture house and municipal theatre on Sergels torg in central Stockholm, with several stages, exhibition halls, a library and rooms available for hire.
locations.facilities: Spaces listed for hire: Foajé 3, Hörsalen, Klarabiografen (cinema), Lilla studion, Studion and the galleries.

locations.name: Langholmen
locations.setting: Former state prison on a small island in central Stockholm, closed in 1975 and converted into a hotel, hostel and restaurant that keeps its original cell wings.
locations.facilities: Hotel, hostel, restaurant and conference rooms in former cell wings

locations.name: Lindholmen
locations.setting: Former shipyard peninsula in Gothenburg redeveloped since the 1990s into a science park of offices, test beds and studios jointly run by the city and industry.

locations.name: Liseberg
locations.setting: Amusement park in central Gothenburg with rides, stages and gardens, plus on-site hotels and dedicated conference and event spaces for hire.
locations.facilities: Conference spaces at the park, Lisebergsbyn and Grand Curiosa Hotel

locations.name: Malmo Live
locations.setting: Concert hall and congress centre in Malmo, home to the Malmo Symphony Orchestra, with a main concert hall and several smaller performance spaces.
locations.logistics: Stage entry at Beringsgatan 5; loading access at Beringsgatan 1-3; visiting address Dag Hammarskjölds torg 4, Malmo.

locations.name: Royal Swedish Opera
locations.setting: National opera and ballet house on Gustav Adolfs torg in Stockholm, founded in 1773, with a 19th-century auditorium due for renovation from 2027.
locations.facilities: The Golden Foyer, the space published for hire, seats up to 120 or holds up to 200 standing, and includes a terrace overlooking Gustav Adolfs torg, weather permitting.

locations.name: Skansen
locations.setting: Open-air museum on Djurgarden in Stockholm, the oldest of its kind in the world, with about 190 historic buildings relocated from across Sweden plus a zoo.
locations.facilities: Business bookings and bookable group experiences

locations.name: Universeum
locations.setting: Sweden's national science centre in Gothenburg, a ten-floor building with rainforest and ocean exhibits, a visualisation dome and dedicated event and conference spaces.
locations.facilities: Published event packages: dinner and drinks in the Ocean zone (max 250), dinner with Wisdome show (max 250), conference (max 30), and hire of the entire venue (over 500).

locations.name: Vasa Museum
locations.setting: Maritime museum on Djurgarden in Stockholm built around the salvaged 17th-century warship Vasa, which sank on its maiden voyage in 1628.
locations.facilities: Ship Hall, the main event space next to the ship Vasa: up to 800 guests seated for dinner or up to 2,000 for a standing reception. Adjoining restaurant: up to 150 guests seated or standing.

locations.name: Visby
locations.setting: Medieval walled town on Gotland and a UNESCO World Heritage site, with a 3.4 kilometre town wall, cobbled lanes and ruined medieval churches.

locations.name: Ystad
locations.setting: Medieval coastal town with half-timbered houses, cobbled streets and a sandy Baltic shoreline, home to the Ystad Studios film facility.

locations.name: Aerospace Bristol
locations.setting: Aviation museum on the former Filton airfield site with a hangar housing a preserved Concorde alongside earlier Bristol-built aircraft.

locations.name: Amberley Museum
locations.setting: Open-air industrial heritage museum on a former chalk quarry near Arundel, with narrow-gauge railways, a lime works, workshops and period industrial buildings.

locations.name: Audley End House and Gardens
locations.setting: Jacobean mansion near Saffron Walden remodelled in the eighteenth century, with state rooms, a service wing and Capability Brown parkland.

locations.name: Barrowland Ballroom
locations.setting: Category B listed 1930s dance hall and live music venue in Glasgow's East End, with its original sprung floor and a neon sign facade on the Gallowgate.

locations.name: Battersea Power Station
locations.setting: Decommissioned Thames-side coal power station with four white chimneys, its turbine halls and boiler house now restored inside a mixed-use redevelopment.
locations.known_for: The King's Speech, Children of Men

locations.name: Beamish Museum
locations.setting: Open-air museum in County Durham recreating a Georgian, Victorian and 1950s north-east England landscape with a working colliery, tramway, town street and farm.

locations.name: Belfast City Hall
locations.setting: Baroque Revival city hall of 1906 in central Belfast, with a domed rotunda, marble entrance hall, council chamber and banqueting hall.

locations.name: Belfast Harbour Studios
locations.setting: Purpose-built film and television studio complex on Belfast's Queen's Island, including the former Paint Hall shipyard building converted into sound stages.

locations.name: Big Pit National Coal Museum
locations.setting: Former working coal mine at Blaenavon in the South Wales valleys, part of a World Heritage industrial landscape, with pithead buildings and an underground tour.

locations.name: Birmingham Hippodrome
locations.setting: Edwardian theatre in Birmingham's Southside, a working proscenium arch auditorium with a fly tower, used for touring opera, ballet and musicals.

locations.name: Bodleian Library
locations.setting: Historic university library in central Oxford with the vaulted Divinity School and Duke Humfrey's medieval reading room, hired for filming by arrangement.
locations.known_for: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets

locations.name: Borough Market
locations.setting: Covered Victorian food market south of London Bridge with wrought-iron arcades, market stalls and surrounding cobbled streets.
locations.known_for: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Bridget Jones's Diary

locations.name: Bressingham Steam and Gardens
locations.setting: Steam preservation site near Diss with narrow-gauge railways, a collection of traction engines and steam locomotives, and surrounding show gardens.

locations.name: Bristol Old Vic
locations.setting: Working eighteenth-century theatre in central Bristol, one of the oldest continuously operating in the English-speaking world, with a Georgian auditorium and backstage spaces.

locations.name: Brooklands Museum
locations.setting: Site of the world's first purpose-built motor racing circuit near Weybridge, with a surviving banked track section, aircraft hangars and early aviation and motoring exhibits.

locations.name: Butser Ancient Farm
locations.setting: Open-air archaeological site near Chalton with reconstructed Iron Age roundhouses, a Roman villa and Anglo-Saxon buildings set in working farmland.

locations.name: Cains Brewery Village
locations.setting: Former Robert Cain brewery complex south of Liverpool city centre, its red brick industrial buildings and courtyards now let as event, retail and filming space.

locations.name: Charlestown Harbour
locations.setting: Small Georgian-era dry-dock harbour near St Austell, still used by tall ships, with quayside cottages and period pilchard cellars around the basin.

locations.name: Cheddar Gorge
locations.setting: England's largest gorge, with 130-metre limestone cliffs, show caves and a clifftop footpath managed as part of the Longleat Estate.

locations.name: Cliveden
locations.setting: Italianate mansion above the Thames at Taplow, now a hotel, with formal parterre gardens, a walled garden and woodland grounds managed by the National Trust.

locations.name: Colne Valley Railway
locations.setting: Heritage standard-gauge railway on the Essex-Suffolk border with a rebuilt country station, signal box and steam and diesel locomotives.

locations.name: Conwy Suspension Bridge
locations.setting: 1826 Thomas Telford suspension bridge across the Conwy estuary in north Wales, beside Conwy Castle, with its original tollhouse kept furnished.

locations.name: Coventry Transport Museum
locations.setting: Museum in central Coventry holding one of the largest collections of British-made cars, motorcycles and bicycles, with large open display halls.

locations.name: Crumlin Road Gaol
locations.setting: Former Victorian prison in north Belfast, closed in 1996, with its radial cell wings, a tunnel to the courthouse and an execution chamber preserved for tours and hire.

locations.name: Dean Clough
locations.setting: Former Crossley's carpet mill complex in Halifax, a chain of Victorian stone mill buildings around courtyards now used as offices, galleries and studios.

locations.name: Digbeth Loc. Studios
locations.setting: Purpose-built television and film studio complex in the Digbeth district of Birmingham with multiple sound stages and production offices.

locations.name: Dyrham Park
locations.setting: Baroque country house near Bath set in a steep deer park, with panelled state rooms, a Delftware collection and a walled garden.

locations.name: Eden Project
locations.setting: Environmental attraction built into a former china clay pit near St Austell, with two giant geodesic biome domes housing rainforest and Mediterranean planting.

locations.name: Elstree Studios
locations.setting: Film and television studio complex at Borehamwood with several sound stages, dating back to the 1920s and long used for major British productions.
locations.known_for: Star Wars, Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade

locations.name: Fort Amherst
locations.setting: Napoleonic-era fortification above Chatham with brick ramparts, gun batteries and a network of tunnels cut into the chalk.

locations.name: Freshwater West
locations.setting: Wide Atlantic surf beach backed by dunes and low cliffs on the open Pembrokeshire coast.
locations.known_for: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part 1, Robin Hood (2010), Their Finest

locations.name: Fulham Palace
locations.setting: Moated former residence of the Bishop of London beside the Thames at Putney, combining Tudor courtyards, Georgian rooms and walled gardens available for filming.

locations.name: Geevor Tin Mine
locations.setting: Former working tin mine on the Cornish coast near Pendeen, with headframes, processing mills, underground tunnels and dressing floors preserved as a museum.

locations.name: Glenfinnan Viaduct
locations.setting: Curved 21-arch concrete railway viaduct of 1901 carrying the West Highland Line above the head of Loch Shiel.
locations.known_for: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban

locations.name: Hylands House
locations.setting: Neoclassical villa near Chelmsford set in landscaped parkland, with Regency reception rooms available for filming and events.

locations.name: Ikon Gallery
locations.setting: Contemporary art gallery in a restored Victorian board school building in Birmingham's Brindleyplace, with galleries, a tower and a public square outside.

locations.name: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum
locations.setting: Red sandstone Edwardian museum and art gallery in Glasgow's West End, with an organ-fitted central hall, galleries and a park setting beside the River Kelvin.

locations.name: Knole
locations.setting: Sprawling calendar house near Sevenoaks with medieval and Tudor courtyards, a deer park and largely unaltered seventeenth-century state rooms.

locations.name: Landguard Fort
locations.setting: Coastal artillery fort at the mouth of the River Orwell near Felixstowe, rebuilt in stages from the seventeenth to the twentieth century with gun casemates and magazines.

locations.name: Loseley Park
locations.setting: Elizabethan mansion near Guildford with panelled state rooms, a walled garden and surrounding parkland, hired for filming.
locations.known_for: Bridget Jones's Diary, The Wedding Date

locations.name: Manchester Central Convention Complex
locations.setting: Former Manchester Central railway station, a wrought iron and glass Victorian train shed converted into an exhibition and convention venue in the city centre.

locations.name: Mitchell Library
locations.setting: Edwardian domed public reference library in Glasgow, one of Europe's largest, with a grand entrance hall, reading rooms and function spaces.

locations.name: Museum of the Gorge, Ironbridge
locations.setting: Former riverside warehouse at Ironbridge, part of the Ironbridge Gorge World Heritage Site of 18th century ironworking remains along the River Severn.

locations.name: National Justice Museum
locations.setting: Former courthouse and prison in Nottingham's Lace Market, with Georgian courtrooms, Victorian cells and a medieval undercroft, now a museum of law and punishment.

locations.name: National Railway Museum
locations.setting: National collection of historic locomotives and rolling stock in York, housed in former railway engine sheds with large open halls and turntables.

locations.name: No.1 Royal Crescent
locations.setting: End-of-terrace Georgian townhouse on Bath's Royal Crescent, restored and furnished as a museum showing how it looked in the 1700s.

locations.name: Old Royal Naval College
locations.setting: Baroque waterfront complex of colonnaded courts and a domed Painted Hall at Greenwich, hired as a stand-in for period Paris, Victorian London and other settings.
locations.known_for: Bridgerton, The Crown, Les Misérables, Thor

locations.name: Orford Ness
locations.setting: Shingle spit on the Suffolk coast used for decades as a secret military testing site, with derelict laboratories, pagoda-shaped test buildings and a lighthouse.

locations.name: Park Hill
locations.setting: Grade II* listed 1960s brutalist housing estate overlooking Sheffield city centre, its long deck-access blocks partly restored and partly awaiting refurbishment.

locations.name: Peterhead Prison Museum
locations.setting: Former Scottish state prison at Peterhead, closed in 2013, with its original cell blocks, exercise yard and perimeter wall open as a museum.

locations.name: Pinewood Studios
locations.setting: Major studio complex west of London whose facilities include large sound stages, the vast 007 Stage, backlots and an underwater filming tank.
locations.known_for: No Time to Die, Star Wars: The Force Awakens
locations.facilities: 30 stages including the 007 Stage (59,092 sq ft, 5,490 m2, 12 m high, with a 91 x 22 m interior tank 2 m deep), an underwater stage with a 20 x 10 x 6 m tank of 1.2 million litres kept at 30 C, three backlots (Paddock Lot, North Lot) with a 32,000 sq ft water pad, workshops of 1,000 to 12,000 sq ft, production offices, hair and makeup rooms, six mixing theatres and 20 cutting rooms.
locations.suitability: Stages are hired individually or in combination; an Indie Film Hub keeps two stages for independent film, over 150 on-lot businesses supply equipment hire, motion capture and 3D scanning, and Diving Services UK manages the underwater stage. Canteen, bar, cinema and 24/7 security on the lot.
locations.logistics: Pinewood Road, Iver Heath: 10 miles from Heathrow, via M4 junction 5 or A40 junction 1; about 45 minutes from Baker Street by Underground to Uxbridge then 10 minutes by taxi, with a free shuttle bus to Uxbridge, Slough, Gerrards Cross and West Ruislip stations; on-site parking.

locations.name: Portmeirion
locations.setting: Italianate village on the Gwynedd coast built by Clough Williams-Ellis between 1925 and 1975, with pastel-coloured buildings, a piazza and subtropical gardens.

locations.name: Portsmouth Historic Dockyard
locations.setting: Working Royal Navy dockyard and heritage site with historic warships, dry docks and Georgian storehouses along Portsmouth Harbour.

locations.name: Racecourse Ground
locations.setting: Football stadium in Wrexham, north Wales, one of the oldest international football grounds still in use, with stands close to the pitch on all four sides.

locations.name: Ribblehead Viaduct
locations.setting: 24-arch stone railway viaduct carrying the Settle to Carlisle line across open moorland in the Yorkshire Dales.

locations.name: Royal Albert Hall
locations.setting: Circular Victorian concert hall with a domed glass and iron roof, tiered galleries and a large stage, available for filming and photography by arrangement.
locations.known_for: The Man Who Knew Too Much, The King's Speech

locations.name: Royal Holloway, University of London
locations.setting: Victorian university campus at Egham centred on the ornate French Renaissance-style Founder's Building, with quadrangles, a chapel and a picture gallery.

locations.name: Salts Mill
locations.setting: Former Victorian textile mill in the Saltaire World Heritage village near Bradford, a vast stone and iron structure now used as galleries, shops and offices.

locations.name: SEC Centre
locations.setting: Exhibition and conference centre on the Clyde in Glasgow, alongside the SSE Hydro concert arena, with large column-free halls used for events and filming.

locations.name: Shepton Mallet Prison
locations.setting: Former English prison dating to 1610, closed in 2013, with cell wings, exercise yards and a gatehouse now hired as an events and filming venue.

locations.name: Snape Maltings
locations.setting: Former Victorian malting complex on the River Alde, its brick maltings and kilns converted into a concert hall, galleries and shops.

locations.name: Somerset House
locations.setting: Neoclassical courtyard building on the Strand with a fountain court and river terrace, hired for events and productions in central London.

locations.name: Southwold Pier
locations.setting: Traditional seaside pier rebuilt in the 2000s on its Edwardian footings, with a pavilion, amusement arcade and end-of-pier walkway over the North Sea.

locations.name: SS Great Britain
locations.setting: Preserved Victorian iron-hulled steamship in her original dry dock in Bristol, with restored decks, engine room and dockside museum buildings.

locations.name: SS Nomadic
locations.setting: Restored 1911 tender ship in Belfast's Hamilton Dock, the last remaining vessel of the White Star Line, moored beside Titanic Belfast as a museum ship.

locations.name: St George's Market
locations.setting: Late Victorian covered market hall in Belfast, a red brick and steel structure with market stalls, used for markets, events and filming when not trading.

locations.name: The Bluecoat
locations.setting: Britain's oldest surviving purpose-built arts centre, a Grade I listed early Georgian charity school building in central Liverpool with galleries, a courtyard and function rooms.

locations.name: The Historic Dockyard Chatham
locations.setting: 80-acre former Royal Navy dockyard on the Medway with Georgian ropewalks, covered slips, dry docks and historic ships used as period maritime backdrops.

locations.name: The Old Truman Brewery
locations.setting: Former East End brewery complex on Brick Lane with converted vat rooms, yards and warehouse floors hired as event and shoot space.

locations.name: The Piece Hall
locations.setting: Grade I listed 18th century cloth hall in Halifax, a colonnaded stone quadrangle of former merchants' rooms around a large open square, now shops, bars and an events space.

locations.name: The Tank Museum
locations.setting: Military vehicle museum on the Bovington army camp with several hundred tanks and armoured vehicles, indoor halls and outdoor arena space.

locations.name: Titan Crane
locations.setting: Cantilever giant crane of 1907 on the Clyde at Clydebank, the last structure standing from the former John Brown shipyard, with a visitor centre inside its base.

locations.name: Tower Bridge
locations.setting: Bascule and suspension bridge over the Thames with twin Victorian Gothic towers and a glass-floored high-level walkway overlooking the city.
locations.known_for: The Mummy Returns, Spider-Man: Far From Home

locations.name: Trades Hall of Glasgow
locations.setting: Robert Adam designed 18th century guild hall in central Glasgow, with a domed saloon and panelled function rooms still used by the city's trade incorporations.

locations.name: Trinity Buoy Wharf
locations.setting: Former lighthouse testing wharf at the mouth of the River Lea, with a lightship, converted shipping-container studios and dockside sheds.

locations.name: Two Temple Place
locations.setting: Neo-Gothic mansion built for William Waldorf Astor beside the Thames, with a galleried great hall and carved wood interiors offered for filming.

locations.name: Utilita Arena Birmingham
locations.setting: Indoor arena in central Birmingham seating several thousand, used for concerts, sport and other large events at the NEC Group's city centre site.

locations.name: V&A Dundee
locations.setting: Waterfront design museum on the Dundee riverside with a stacked-stone exterior by architect Kengo Kuma, opened in 2018 beside the historic ship RRS Discovery.

locations.name: Victoria Baths
locations.setting: Disused Edwardian public baths in Manchester with three original pools, a Turkish suite and stained glass, hired as a filming location since its closure in 1993.

locations.name: Wales Millennium Centre
locations.setting: Steel and slate clad performing arts centre on Cardiff Bay, with a main theatre, studio spaces and a bronze-lettered curved facade.

locations.name: Wilton's Music Hall
locations.setting: Surviving Victorian music hall in Wapping with a barley-twist column auditorium and worn brick backstage areas, hired for filming and photography.

locations.name: Wrest Park
locations.setting: Country house near Silsoe built in French chateau style, set within formal gardens with canals, pavilions and woodland walks.
